source_text: Sicut per unum hominem peccatum in hunc mundum intravit et per peccatum mors, ita et per unum Iesum Christum gratia et donum in plures abundavit. Gloria Christo. Amen.
thought_title: Sin and death through one man, grace through one Christ
orientation: Origen is summarizing the contrast between Adam's transgression and the overflowing grace that comes through Jesus Christ.
pass_a_gloss: Just as through one man sin entered into this world and through sin death, so also through one Jesus Christ grace and gift abounded unto many. Glory to Christ. Amen.

choices.why: The demonstrative hunc is explicit in the source and should be kept.
The source names Jesus Christ explicitly, not just Christ.
Both nouns are distinct in the source and should remain separate.
The preposition in with accusative here has a directional sense of reaching many.

bible_refs.note: per unum hominem peccatum in hunc mundum intravit et per peccatum mors
gratia et donum in plures abundavit

pass_b_english: Just as sin entered this world through one man, and death through sin, so also grace and gift abounded unto many through one Jesus Christ (Romans 5:12b-15). Glory to Christ. Amen.

problems.source_quote: Sicut per unum hominem peccatum in hunc mundum intravit et per peccatum mors, ita et per unum Iesum Christum gratia et donum in plures abundavit
problems.why: The citation combines two verses but the Latin quotes only one continuous passage; 5:12b-15 is more accurate.
problems.ruling: Latin conflates Romans 5:12 and 5:15 wording; citation '(5:12, 15)' is acceptable but '5:12b-15' more precise.

fixed: The citation combines two verses but the Latin quotes only one continuous passage; 5:12b-15 is more accurate.

refereed.why: English drops "unum" ("one"), which parallels "unum hominem" and is theologically crucial to Paul's argument about the one man and the one Christ.
refereed.ruling: English omits 'unum' in 'per unum Iesum Christum', losing the crucial parallel with 'unum hominem'.
